newsitem.title: USA: Canada LPG market continued to tumble in week.
newsitem.headline: Canada LPG market continued to tumble in week.

text.p: Canada liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) continued to tumble this week on the heels of falling prices in the U.S. but some players said there was still concern over inventories.
In what players said was moderate trade this week, spot propane in the eastern hub of Sarnia dropped 5.75 cents from last Thursday to between 54.00 cents and 55.25 cents a gallon.
Players said the downtrend is likely continue although contractual inventories for the material look tight.
"People are still nervous over their contractual inventories but once we get into late February the writing will be on the wall," said one Sarnia trader.
The new contractual year in Canada begins after March 31 and some players worry if the weathers turn very cold in February inventories may be too low to meet demand.

Another player, however, said such concerns arise every year. "This happens every year. It's too early to tell whether we will have a shortage of inventory again this year," said the Edmonton player in western Canada.
Spot propane prices in Edmonton also dropped 7.00 cents to between 44.00/44.25 cents, with deals done in both ranges.
The butane markets remained relatively quiet amid little demand, with Sarnia normal down about a half cent. --((Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631))
